subject.title: fix(agents): avoid symlink-follow in auth.json bootstrap

question: Should OpenClaw merge and own this generic no-final-path-chmod/exact-mode wrapper now, or should the security guarantee be added and released from `@openclaw/fs-safe` before this PR lands?
rationale: The remaining question is not whether the reproduced symlink path needs hardening, but which layer permanently owns a generic replacement and permission contract affecting all OpenClaw callers.

options.title: Move the guarantee into fs-safe first
options.body: Add and release a descriptor-based exact-mode/no-final-path-chmod contract in `@openclaw/fs-safe`, then reduce OpenClaw back to delegation.

options.title: Approve the local wrapper as a temporary owner
options.body: Merge the proven wrapper now with an explicit follow-up to converge on an fs-safe API and avoid permanent behavior drift.

options.title: Pause the hardening path
options.body: Keep this PR open until security owners decide that the affected parent-directory threat model warrants one of the two supported ownership paths.

recommendation.title: Move the guarantee into fs-safe first
recommendation.body: Add and release a descriptor-based exact-mode/no-final-path-chmod contract in `@openclaw/fs-safe`, then reduce OpenClaw back to delegation.

likelyOwner.reason: This group was directly asked to approve the remaining security and dependency-boundary choice.
